purpose: Teach: 宅地/本数/常々/急行/チャージ/有給/待ち時間/少額

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 蓮、不動産業界、宅地動向、君も、関心を持て、社会人として、当然だぞ。
lines.en: Ren — the real estate industry, residential trends — you need to take an interest. That's what it means to be an adult.
lines.style: Measured and direct. Opens with the name like a teacher calling on a student. Steady cadence. The weight of expectation is clear but not unkind — this is guidance, not criticism.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。研究論文の本数、年々、増やしていけるよう、頑張ってまいります、絶対。
lines.en: Yes. I'll work to increase the number of papers I publish each year. I promise.
lines.style: Formal bow in the voice. Quick intake at the start to signal readiness. Earnest but not panicked — the conviction of someone who means what they're saying. Slight emphasis on the final promise.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 常々、君のことを、評価しているぞ、研究、続けていけ、本気で、絶対だ、絶対。
lines.en: I've always valued your work, Ren. Keep pursuing your research. Seriously — you can do this.
lines.style: Warm but still composed. The praise lands softly; he's not used to giving it loosely. Slight lean forward on 「君のことを」— personal acknowledgment beneath the formality. The repetition carries conviction, not doubt.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。学会、急行で、向かいます、本気で、発表、絶対、成功させたいです、絶対に。
lines.en: Yes. I'm heading to the conference right away. I'm going to give this presentation everything I have — I absolutely will succeed.
lines.style: Voice lifts with resolve. Quick breath before the commitment. The repetition of 「絶対」 builds momentum rather than sounding frantic — this is a declaration. Steady eye contact in the tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 研究費、無駄な、チャージ、絶対、しないように、慎重に、扱え、絶対だぞ、絶対。
lines.en: With research funds, don't be careless about unnecessary expenses. Handle everything with care. That's non-negotiable.
lines.style: Shifts to advisory mode — less warmth, more precision. Each instruction lands individually. The repetition at the end is firm but not harsh — this is about responsibility, not blame. A mentor protecting his researcher.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。有給休暇、研究の合間、しっかり、取らせていただきます、感謝しております、絶対。
lines.en: Yes. I'll make sure to take my paid leave during breaks in the research schedule. I'm truly grateful for your support.
lines.style: Respectful but less formal than before — he's relaxing slightly into trust. Gentle emphasis on the gratitude. No rush; he's speaking from genuine appreciation, not obligation. Small trailing acknowledgment.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 実験の待ち時間、効率化できる方法、君も、考えてみろ、若い視点、大事だぞ。
lines.en: During the experimental waiting periods, think about ways to make the process more efficient. Your perspective as someone younger is valuable.
lines.style: Shifts into collaborative mode — this is less instruction, more invitation. Opens with the problem, then trusts him to contribute. Warmth returns. The final phrase carries real respect — not flattery, but recognition.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。少額の研究助成、申請、検討しております、本当に、ありがたいです、本気で、絶対。
lines.en: Yes. I'm looking into applying for smaller research grants. I truly appreciate the opportunities you're giving me.
lines.style: Formal gratitude with genuine feeling underneath. Breath caught at the start — he's managing emotion here, the recognition of support matters. The final emphasis is soft but sincere. This is a moment of real connection within the hierarchy.
